findings.title: resync_status left permanently true when if/loop resync exits via 'return true' on T_END, silently suppressing all subsequent error reports
findings.description: resync_parser() sets resync_status=true at entry (line 2623) and only ever resets it to false at line 3044 (after the first switch) and line 3285 (end of function). In case S_IF_STATEMENT, if the resync loop encounters T_END it executes `return true;` directly (line 2942) instead of `break;`ing out of the switch — this is a genuine function return, bypassing both reset points entirely. The identical pattern exists in case S_LOOP_STATEMENT (line 2976). Once this path is taken, resync_status stays true for the rest of the parse. generate_error_report(...) (both overloads, lines 72 and 97) gate all message construction behind `if (!resync_status)`, so every subsequent call becomes a silent no-op — no more diagnostics are ever added to error_reports, even though `errors_occured` (set independently at each call site) keeps getting set correctly. This path is not a rare corner case: it is exactly what happens on the extremely common mistake of a missing ';' before the closing 'end if'/'end loop' of a statement (parse_if_statement/parse_loop_statement call resync_parser(state) at parser.cpp:1706/1733 and 1834/1860 precisely when a statement inside the body isn't followed by ';', and the very next real token is frequently 'end').

findings.title: clear_error_reports() wipes ALL previously accumulated parse errors when an unterminated string literal is hit
findings.description: In parse_factor(), when a T_STRING_VALUE token is produced with Lexer->quote_status still true (meaning the string ran to EOF without a closing quote), the code calls `clear_error_reports()` before adding a single 'quotation left open' message. clear_error_reports() (parser.cpp:112-115) does `error_reports.clear()`, discarding every error message accumulated over the entire file up to that point — missing semicolons, missing keywords, type errors, etc. The user only ever sees the final 'quotation left open' message (plus anything reported afterward); all earlier legitimate diagnostics are silently lost. This directly contradicts the handout's requirement for 'meaningful errors'.

findings.title: resync_parser returns an uninitialized bool for the (common) S_PROCEDURE_BODY resync path
findings.description: `bool return_state;` is declared without an initializer at parser.cpp:2625. In the first switch, case S_PROCEDURE_BODY's while loop (lines 2771-2872) sets `new_state = original_state` (i.e. S_PROCEDURE_BODY again) and breaks whenever it immediately sees T_BEGIN/T_END/T_PROCEDURE (lines 2775-2789) or finds a semicolon while scanning (lines 2862-2869) — these are the first-checked, most common exits from the loop. Control then falls into the second switch's `case S_PROCEDURE_BODY:` (lines 3132-3136), whose body is empty — it never assigns return_state. The function then executes `return return_state;` at line 3286, returning an indeterminate/garbage boolean. Every call site that invokes resync_parser with state=S_PROCEDURE_BODY (parser.cpp:556,583,602,625,647,662,674, inside parse_procedure_body) assigns this to `valid_parse` and branches on it afterward. This is asymmetric with the analogous S_PROGRAM_BODY case (lines 3060-3064), which correctly does `return_state = true;`.
findings.evidence:
parser.cpp:2625 `bool return_state;` (no initializer); parser.cpp:3132-3136:
`    //9
    case S_PROCEDURE_BODY:

        break;
` — no assignment to return_state; parser.cpp:3286 `return return_state;`

findings.title: Second dispatch switch reads an uninitialized parser_state (`new_state`) for 23 of 28 enum values whose first-switch case bodies are empty
findings.description: `parser_state new_state;` is declared without an initializer at line 2627. Only 5 of the 28 first-switch cases (S_PROGRAM_BODY, S_PROCEDURE_HEADER, S_PROCEDURE_BODY, S_IF_STATEMENT, S_LOOP_STATEMENT) actually assign new_state; the remaining 23 cases (S_PROGRAM, S_PROGRAM_HEADER, S_BASE_DECLARATION, S_PROCEDURE_DECLARATION, S_PARAMETER_LIST, S_PARAMETER, S_VARIABLE_DECLARATION, S_TYPE_DECLARATION, S_TYPE_MARK, S_BOUND, S_BASE_STATEMENT, S_PROCEDURE_CALL, S_ASSIGNMENT_STATMENT, S_ASSIGNMENT_DESTINATION, S_RETURN_STATEMENT, S_EXPRESSION, S_ARITH_OP, S_RELATION, S_TERM, S_FACTOR, S_NAME, S_ARGUMENT_LIST, S_NUMBER) are simply `case X: break;` with no synchronizing-token logic at all. If resync_parser is ever called with one of these states, the second switch (line 3046) dispatches on an uninitialized enum value, which is undefined behavior (could match an arbitrary case, calling the wrong parse_* function, or hit default). I confirmed via grep that every current call site in parser.cpp only ever passes S_PROGRAM_BODY, S_PROCEDURE_BODY, S_IF_STATEMENT, or S_LOOP_STATEMENT (directly, or recursively via `original_state` which is always one of those), so this specific UB is not currently triggered — but it means ~82% of the parser_state enum, covering expressions/terms/factors/names/arguments/procedure calls/assignments/returns/parameters/bounds/type marks, has no dedicated synchronizing-token set defined despite the enum apparently being designed for that purpose, and represents a latent trap for any future call site added with one of these states.
findings.evidence:
e.g. parser.cpp:3018-3021 `//25
    case S_FACTOR:

        break;` in the second switch, paired with the equally empty first-switch case at parser.cpp:3019-3021. `grep -n 'parser_state state =' parser.cpp` combined with `grep -n resync_parser` shows only S_PROGRAM_BODY/S_PROCEDURE_BODY/S_IF_STATEMENT/S_LOOP_STATEMENT are ever used as call-site states.

findings.title: Missing `break` after T_TYPE branch in S_PROGRAM_BODY resync case lets new_state be silently discarded/overwritten
findings.description: In case S_PROGRAM_BODY's resync loop, the T_PROCEDURE and T_VARIABLE branches (lines 2693-2702) both set `new_state = S_BASE_DECLARATION;` and `break;`. The T_TYPE branch (lines 2703-2706) sets `new_state = S_BASE_DECLARATION;` but has NO break, so execution falls through into the STATEMENTS checks (2708-2730) and then unconditionally executes `Current_parse_token = Get_Valid_Token();` (line 2733), consuming an extra token before possibly looping again — meaning the intended 'we found a type keyword, dispatch to base declaration' result can be silently overwritten on a later loop iteration or discarded. This is inconsistent with the otherwise-identical S_PROCEDURE_BODY case, where the analogous T_TYPE branch (lines 2832-2836) DOES include `break;`, indicating this is a plain omission rather than intentional design.

findings.title: generate_error_report's 'first token on line -> blame previous line' heuristic misattributes line numbers for 'wrong token' diagnostics, not just 'missing token' diagnostics
findings.description: generate_error_report(string) unconditionally applies: if Current_parse_token.first_token_on_line, report prev_token.line_found, else report Current_parse_token.line_found. This heuristic is appropriate for 'missing terminator' messages (e.g. missing ';') where the omission logically belongs at the end of the previous line. But the same function is also called for diagnostics where Current_parse_token itself IS the erroneous token (e.g. parser.cpp:168 'Expected keyword "Program" not found', parser.cpp:187 'Expected "identifier" not found', parser.cpp:202 'Expected keyword "is" is not found'). If that bad token happens to be the first token on a new source line, the error is reported on the PREVIOUS line instead of the line the bad token actually appears on.

findings.title: Typechecker error line numbers use the scanner's live read cursor (Lexer->current_line) instead of the offending token's stored line_found, producing off-by-N-lines errors
findings.description: generate_error_report(std::string, int line_number) (parser.cpp:94-110, in scope as the sink) is called from Typechecker.cpp with `parser_parent->Lexer->current_line` as the line number (e.g. Typechecker.cpp:331,361,386,408,514,536,565,593,1221,1305, and 286). Lexer->current_line (scanner.h:94) is a live cursor incremented as the scanner scans raw characters (scanner.cpp:395-396, 470-471), and is completely decoupled from any specific token's own `line_found` (which is fixed at token-creation time, scanner.cpp:232/406/414/445/452/531). Because the parser always holds a 1-token lookahead (Current_parse_token + Next_parse_token, both already pulled from the scanner) and typechecking of an expression/relation runs only after the whole expression/statement has been parsed, Lexer->current_line at typecheck time reflects wherever the scanner has already read ahead to — not the line of the operands actually being checked. This is corroborated by a comment directly above the correct fix at Typechecker.cpp:285: `// line_error = second_token.line_found;` immediately followed by the actual (buggy) code at line 286: `line_error = parser_parent->Lexer->current_line;` — i.e. the developer had the correct approach available and used the cursor-based one instead.
findings.evidence: Typechecker.cpp:285-286: `// line_error = second_token.line_found;\n        line_error = parser_parent->Lexer->current_line;` ; Typechecker.cpp:331 `parser_parent->generate_error_report("Arithmetic operations must be between floats and integers", parser_parent->Lexer->current_line);` ; sink defined at parser.cpp:94-110.

findings.title: First token/error of a file can be misreported as 'Error on line 0'
findings.description: Get_Valid_Token()'s 'first token' branch (Current_parse_token.type == 9999, lines 35-41) never assigns `prev_token`; prev_token is only ever set in the 'else' branch (line 45). token::line_found defaults to 0 (token.h:108, and constructor at token.h:95). scanner::last_sent_token (scanner.h:140) is likewise default-constructed with line_found=0 before any token is scanned, so for the very first token in any file, scanner.cpp:191 `if (Current_token->line_found != last_sent_token.line_found)` compares the real line (>=1) against 0 and always sets first_token_on_line=true for token #1. If the very first error in the file occurs on that first token (e.g. a file that doesn't start with the 'Program' keyword, triggering generate_error_report at parser.cpp:168), generate_error_report's heuristic (parser.cpp:76-79) takes the `first_token_on_line` branch and reports `prev_token.line_found`, which is still its default value of 0 — producing 'Error on line 0' instead of line 1 (or wherever the token actually is).
findings.evidence: parser.cpp:35-41 (no prev_token assignment on first token); token.h:108 `int line_found = 0;`; scanner.h:140 `token last_sent_token;`; scanner.cpp:191 `if (Current_token->line_found != last_sent_token.line_found) { Current_token->first_token_on_line = true; }`; parser.cpp:78 `full_error_message = "Error on line " + std::to_string(prev_token.line_found) + ": ";`

findings.title: Recursive resync_parser() return value discarded for S_BASE_DECLARATION and S_PROCEDURE_DECLARATION, unlike sibling cases
findings.description: In the second switch, when a freshly-parsed base declaration or procedure declaration isn't followed by the expected terminator, the code recurses: `resync_parser(original_state);` at line 3080 (case S_BASE_DECLARATION) and line 3102 (case S_PROCEDURE_DECLARATION) — but the return value is NOT captured back into `return_state`, so return_state keeps whatever value it held from the earlier `parse_base_declaration()`/`parse_procedure_declaration()` call (typically true, since we're inside the `if (return_state)` branch). This is inconsistent with the parallel cases S_VARIABLE_DECLARATION (line 3150), S_TYPE_DECLARATION (line 3172), and S_BASE_STATEMENT (line 3204), which all correctly do `return_state = resync_parser(original_state);`. As written, resync_parser can report overall success (true) for a base/procedure declaration resync even when the nested recursive resync attempt actually failed.

findings.title: main() always returns exit code 0 regardless of parse success/failure — process exit status never reflects a failed parse
findings.description: The parser constructor (parser.cpp:3-28) determines pass/fail/errors-present state and only prints text to stdout ('The program had parsing errors' / 'parsed successfully with errors' / 'parsed successfully with no errors') via print_errors()/std::cout — it never returns or stores this status anywhere main() can observe. main() (main.cpp:10-31) always does `return 0;` (line 29) after constructing the parser, regardless of whether parsing failed or errors were reported; the only non-zero exit path is 'no file argument given' (line 16, returns 1). Any build system, test harness, or CI pipeline relying on the process exit code to detect a failed/erroring compile will incorrectly see success (exit 0) for every malformed input file, defeating the purpose of 'meaningful errors' from an automation perspective.

findings.title: Get_Valid_Token silently discards out-of-range/'junk' tokens with no diagnostic, and the discard filter is not applied to the initial two tokens fetched at start
findings.description: In Get_Valid_Token()'s 'not first token' branch, `while (Next_parse_token_type > T_INVALID || Next_parse_token_type < 0) { Next_parse_token = Lexer->Get_token(); ... }` (lines 52-56) repeatedly re-fetches from the scanner whenever it returns a token whose type is out of the valid range, silently dropping it — the adjacent comment ('for some reason random junk sometimes appears') indicates this is a known scanner quirk being papered over, but no error is ever reported for the discarded token, so potentially real lexical problems are hidden from the user. Additionally, this filtering loop only runs in the 'else' branch; the very first two tokens fetched during initialization (lines 37-38, `Current_parse_token = Lexer->Get_token(); Next_parse_token = Lexer->Get_token();`) are not passed through any such filter, so a garbage-typed token could become Current_parse_token or the initial Next_parse_token unfiltered.

findings.title: S_PARAMETER_LIST resync dispatch uses a literal "ERROR" string as a real procedure name and unconditionally calls two unrelated parse functions back to back
findings.description: In the second switch's case S_PARAMETER_LIST (reached when S_PROCEDURE_BODY resync detects a T_VARIABLE token immediately after T_LPARAM), the code does `return_state = parse_parameter_list("ERROR"); return_state = parse_procedure_body();` — passing the literal string "ERROR" as if it were a genuine procedure name (used elsewhere for symbol-table scoping via procedure_name parameters), then unconditionally invoking parse_procedure_body() immediately after regardless of whether parse_parameter_list succeeded, discarding its return_state. The preceding comment `//THESE USED STILL?` (line 3121) signals the original author's own uncertainty about whether this code path is even exercised/maintained correctly.

findings.title: parse_if_statement continues to the next mandatory-token check after resync without validating where resync actually left the cursor, risking cascading spurious errors from a single mistake
findings.description: After a missing ')' error, `valid_parse = resync_parser(state);` (line 1668) is called, and execution unconditionally falls through to the next check `if (Current_parse_token_type == T_THEN)` (line 1671) without verifying that resync actually landed at/near a 'then' keyword. resync_parser(S_IF_STATEMENT) can legitimately land on tokens like T_IF/T_FOR/T_RETURN/T_IDENTIFIER (parser.cpp:2918-2948) that begin a nested statement, not a 'then'. In that case, the immediately following T_THEN check fails, generating a second, likely-spurious 'Missing expected keyword "then"' error (line 1677) and triggering yet another resync (line 1679) for what may really be a single underlying mistake — producing a cascade of confusing diagnostics for the user rather than one clear message.
findings.evidence: parser.cpp:1660-1680: after `valid_parse = resync_parser(state);` (1668) there is no check of what token resync actually stopped on before immediately testing `if (Current_parse_token_type == T_THEN)` (1671) and issuing a second error/resync (1677-1679) if it doesn't match.

notes:
Scope covered: parser.cpp lines 1-160 (Get_Valid_Token, generate_error_report x2, add/clear_error_reports, print_errors, parser ctor), the parser_state enum (parser.h:12-42), and the complete resync_parser function (parser.cpp:2620-3287, both switch statements in full). Also cross-checked every call site of resync_parser and every `parser_state state = ...` assignment via grep to determine which states are actually reachable at runtime, and cross-checked Typechecker.cpp's use of the in-scope generate_error_report(msg, line) overload per the task's specific hint about Lexer->current_line.

Key confirmed, non-speculative, high-confidence findings (in priority order):
1. resync_status is left stuck `true` forever (suppressing ALL subsequent error messages) whenever if/loop-statement resync hits T_END and takes the early `return true;` at parser.cpp:2942/2976, bypassing the only two `resync_status = false;` reset points (lines 3044, 3285). This is reachable via the very common case of a missing ';' before 'end if'/'end loop'.
2. `clear_error_reports()` at parser.cpp:2446 wipes the entire accumulated error_reports vector whenever an unterminated string literal is found, discarding all prior legitimate diagnostics.
3. `return_state` (parser.cpp:2625, uninitialized) is returned as garbage for the S_PROCEDURE_BODY resync path because the corresponding second-switch case (3133-3136) is empty, unlike the parallel, correctly-handled S_PROGRAM_BODY case.
4. Only 5 of 28 parser_state enum values have any synchronizing-token logic in resync_parser's first switch; the rest leave `new_state` (parser.cpp:2627) uninitialized, which would be UB if ever dispatched — confirmed currently unreachable via existing call sites (only S_PROGRAM_BODY/S_PROCEDURE_BODY/S_IF_STATEMENT/S_LOOP_STATEMENT are ever passed), but represents an almost-entirely-vestigial per-construct resync design (no fine-grained recovery for expressions/terms/factors/names/parameters/etc.).
5. Missing `break` after the T_TYPE branch in the S_PROGRAM_BODY case (parser.cpp:2703-2706), inconsistent with the otherwise identical, correctly-`break`-ed T_PROCEDURE/T_VARIABLE branches and the analogous T_TYPE branch in S_PROCEDURE_BODY.
6/7/8. Three distinct, independently-confirmed line-number reporting bugs: (a) parser.cpp's single-arg generate_error_report misattributes 'wrong token' errors to the previous line when applying its 'missing terminator' heuristic; (b) Typechecker.cpp uses the scanner's live `current_line` cursor (not the offending token's `line_found`) for ~11 semantic error sites, with direct evidence of a commented-out correct implementation at Typechecker.cpp:285; (c) the very first error in a file can be misreported as line 0 due to prev_token/last_sent_token default-initialization interacting with the first_token_on_line heuristic.
9. resync_parser's recursive call for S_BASE_DECLARATION/S_PROCEDURE_DECLARATION (parser.cpp:3080,3102) discards its own return value, unlike the parallel S_VARIABLE_DECLARATION/S_TYPE_DECLARATION/S_BASE_STATEMENT cases.
10. main.cpp always returns 0 on any parse outcome; only a missing file argument produces a non-zero exit code — confirmed the parser class never surfaces pass/fail status beyond console text.

Lower-confidence/speculative findings included for completeness (marked speculative:true): the practical UB-if-reached risk of unhandled parser_state cases; silent junk-token discarding in Get_Valid_Token without diagnostics and its asymmetric application to the initial two tokens; the "ERROR" placeholder-string + unconditional double-dispatch in the S_PARAMETER_LIST resync case; and the lack of landing-token validation in parse_if_statement after resync potentially cascading spurious errors.

Did not deeply audit parse_base_declaration/parse_base_statement/expression-family internals themselves (out of assigned scope), only their interaction with the error-handling/resync subsystem. Did not execute/compile the code — all findings are derived from static reading of parser.cpp, parser.h, relevant scanner.cpp/scanner.h/token.h defaults, and the specific Typechecker.cpp call sites into the in-scope generate_error_report(msg,int) sink.
